title: A nontrivial finite purely inseparable extension has a degree-p intermediate step
statement: Let $L/K$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] of characteristic $p>0$ with $[L:K]>1$. Then there are an intermediate field $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ and an element $z\in L$ such that $M/K$ is a finite purely inseparable extension, $[M:K]<[L:K]$, $L=M(z)$, $z^p=f$ for some $f\in M$, and $[L:M]=p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, induction paragraph: choose $K\subset M\subset L$ with $L/M$ a degree-$p$ extension obtained by adjoining a $p$th root

proof.text: (The last step of a $p$th-root tower.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] to $F=K$, $E=L$ (a finite purely inseparable extension of a field of characteristic $p$): there are $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\in L$ with $L=K(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ such that, with $K_{i}=K(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i})$ ($K_0=K$), for each $i=1,\dots,n$ we have $\alpha_i^p\in K_{i-1}$ and $[K_{i-1}(\alpha_i):K_{i-1}]=p$. If $n=0$ then $L=K_0=K$ and $[L:K]=1$, against the hypothesis $[L:K]>1$; so $n\ge1$. Put $M=K_{n-1}$, $z=\alpha_n$ and $f=z^p$. Then $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ is an intermediate field, $f=\alpha_n^p\in K_{n-1}=M$, $M(z)=K(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{n-1})(\alpha_n)=K(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)=L$, and the clause $i=n$ gives $[L:M]=[K_{n-1}(\alpha_n):K_{n-1}]=p$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable), statement; used in More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, 'Let K subset M subset L be a subfield such that L is a degree p extension of M obtained by adjoining a pth root of an element f in M'

proof.text: ($M/K$ is finite purely inseparable.) $M$ is a $K$-linear subspace of the finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $L$, hence finite-dimensional over $K$. Every $\beta\in M$ is an element of $L$, so by the definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] applied to $L/K$ there is $n\ge0$ with $\beta^{p^n}\in K$; hence every element of $M$ is purely inseparable over $K$, and $M/K$ is finite purely inseparable by the same definition.

source.place: Fields, Definition Tag 09HE (definition-purely-inseparable); used in More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PR, proof ('Since A subset B subset C are finite and L/M/K are purely inseparable')

proof.text: ($[M:K]<[L:K]$.) The extensions $M/K$ (Step 2) and $L/M$ ($[L:M]=p$, Step 1) are finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] applied to $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ gives $[L:K]=[L:M]\,[M:K]=p\,[M:K]$. As $p\ge2$ and $[M:K]\ge1$, $[L:K]=p[M:K]\ge2[M:K]>[M:K]$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_degree_p_intermediate (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite K L] [IsPurelyInseparable K L] (p : ℕ) [CharP K p] (hp : 0 < p) (hdeg : 1 < Module.finrank K L) : ∃ (M : IntermediateField K L) (z : L), Module.Finite K M ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K M ∧ Module.finrank K M < Module.finrank K L ∧ IntermediateField.adjoin M ({z} : Set L) = ⊤ ∧ (∃ f : M, z ^ p = (f : L)) ∧ Module.finrank M L = p
